hints.content: In order to find $F'(-1)$, we should first find an expression for $F'(x)$ (for any input $x$) in terms of $f$, $g$, and their derivatives.

So $F'(x)=\dfrac{f'(x)g(x)-f(x)g'(x)}{[g(x)]^2}$.

We can now plug $x=-1$ into this expression:

$F'(-1)=\dfrac{f'(-1)g(-1)-f(-1)g'(-1)}{[g(-1)]^2}$

We are given that $f(-1)=3$ and $f'(-1)=5$.

Since $g(x)=2x^3$, we know that $g(-1)=-2$ and $g'(-1)=6$. [[☃ explanation 1]]

Let's plug in those values!

$\begin{align}
F'(-1)&=\dfrac{(5)(-2)-(3)(6)}{(-2)^2}
\\\\
&=\dfrac{-28}{4}
\\\\
&=-7
\end{align}$

### Finding $g(-1)$

>$\begin{align}
g(\blueD{-1})&=2(\blueD{-1})^3
\\\\\\\\
&=-2
\end{align}$

### Finding $g'(x)$

>$\begin{align}
g'(x)&=\dfrac{d}{dx}(2x^3)
\\\\\\\\
&=2\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^3)
\\\\\\\\
&=2(3x^2)
\\\\\\
&=6x^2
\end{align}$

### Finding $g'(-1)$

>$\begin{align}
g'(\blueD{-1})&=6(\blueD{-1})^2
\\\\\\\\
&=6
\end{align}$
